Only after that sleep does it read the title and caption it reports on. INT-002 runs inspect with `--settle 150` (tests/integration.test.mjs:96). Inspect sleeps with `page.waitForTimeout(settle)` (scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs:26) before collecting diagnostics and screenshots. The test then asserts on that fixed interval (`step.captured - step.arrived &gt;= 150`, line 102) instead of on a settled signal. So the &#39;use no fixed sleeps&#39; clause is not met. Judges A and B argued pass because the tests contain no `waitForTimeout` and the scripts poll `data-step-index`. The cited material shows that index polling sits next to the fixed sleeps and does not replace them. The browser the tests drive still waits a fixed number of milliseconds for the transition before the content assertions run. The tests not calling Playwright directly does not remove those sleeps from the browser tests. Their point that the 10 ms `setTimeout` in contracts.test.tsx is a jsdom act flush, not a browser test, is correct, but that is not the basis of this fail.tests/integration.test.mjs:96 INT-002 runs `npm run inspect -- fixture --settle 150`; line 102 asserts `step.captured - step.arrived &gt;= 150`, which tests a fixed-time wait, not observable settled … | scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs:24-31: after `stepIndex`, it calls `await page.waitForTimeout(settle)` before diagnostics and the screenshot | tests/integration.test.mjs:125-128 E2E-001 runs `npm run verify` and asserts the PASS step lines and the sample validation | scripts/verify.mjs:37-45: `await page.waitForTimeout(SETTLE_MS)` after `stepIndex` and before reading `[data-presentation-title]` and `[data-presentation-caption]` | scripts/browser-tools.mjs:7 `export const SETTLE_MS = 850`, a fixed sleep duration | quoted lines: tests/integration.test.mjs:96-110 | quoted lines: tests/integration.test.mjs:116-133 | quoted lines: scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs:23-33 | quoted lines: scripts/verify.mjs:34-47 | quoted lines: scripts/browser-tools.mjs:7-7 | decider ruling: fail, confirmed by the closed-world span audit | judging basis: decider-fail | tests/integration.test.mjs | scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs | scripts/verify.mjs | scripts/browser-tools.mjs
engineering-tests-isolate-resourcesengineering-presentation-code-and-tests0.375 of 0.375 (minor)passEvery test that starts a preview or browser runs the scripts, and `freePort()` in browser-tools.mjs allocates a dynamic port by listening on port 0. No fixed port is shared. The scripts own the Vite process directly and always close it. integration.test.mjs `assertStopped` then checks that the Chromium and preview PIDs no longer exist (`process.kill(pid, 0)` throws ESRCH) and that the preview URL is unreachable. This is checked on success, on every injected-failure case (E2E-002) and in the INT-002 inspect run, so no preview is left behind. In Stage.tsx the remount `serial` only increments when `Scene`, `groupKey`, or (for ungrouped steps) `id` changes. The `motion.div` is keyed by `identity.serial`. Moving between adjacent steps in the same group therefore keeps the same host and updates the existing scene with the new `payload.beat`, with no remount. A single shared groupKey is the correct grouping for this one evolving scene. tiebreaks{"demo-integration":null,"scene-kit":null,"presentation-skill":null,"verification-tooling":null,"engineering-quality":{"ok":true,"criteria":["engineering-tests-wait-on-state"],"inventory_kind":"neutral source","attempts":[{"stage":"tiebreak","attempt":1,"ok":true,"error":null}],"first_results":[{"id":"engineering-tests-wait-on-state","verdict":"fail","rationale":"The requirement says browser-driving tests must wait for observable state and use no fixed sleeps. The delivered tests drive Chromium only by spawning the verify and inspect scripts, and that browser path sleeps for a fixed time. E2E-001 runs `npm run verify` (tests/integration.test.mjs:125). It then asserts the per-step PASS lines and the title/caption sample validation that verify prints. Inside verify, each step polls `stepIndex` and then calls `page.waitForTimeout(SETTLE_MS)` (scripts/verify.mjs:39), a fixed 850 ms (scripts/browser-tools.mjs:7). Only after that sleep does it read the title and caption it reports on. INT-002 runs inspect with `--settle 150` (tests/integration.test.mjs:96). Inspect sleeps with `page.waitForTimeout(settle)` (scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs:26) before collecting diagnostics and screenshots. The test then asserts on that fixed interval (`step.captured - step.arrived &gt;= 150`, line 102) instead of on a settled signal. So the &#39;use no fixed sleeps&#39; clause is not met. Judges A and B argued pass because the tests contain no `waitForTimeout` and the scripts poll `data-step-index`. The cited material shows that index polling sits next to the fixed sleeps and does not replace them. The browser the tests drive still waits a fixed number of milliseconds for the transition before the content assertions run. The tests not calling Playwright directly does not remove those sleeps from the browser tests. Inside verify, each step polls `stepIndex` and then calls `page.waitForTimeout(SETTLE_MS)` (scripts/verify.mjs:39), a fixed 850 ms (scripts/browser-tools.mjs:7). The cited material shows that index polling sits next to the fixed sleeps and does not replace them. The browser the tests drive still waits a fixed number of milliseconds for the transition before the content assertions run.
